entries.name: Feature: Witherbloom Initiate
entries: You gain the {@feat Strixhaven Initiate|SCC} feat and must choose Witherbloom within it.

In addition, if you have the Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature, the spells on the Witherbloom Spells table are added to the spell list of your spellcasting class. (If you are a multiclass character with multiple spell lists, these spells are added to all of them.)

entries.caption: Witherbloom Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell Cure Wounds}, {@spell Inflict Wounds}
2nd
{@spell Lesser Restoration}, {@spell Wither and Bloom|SCC}
3rd
{@spell Revivify}, {@spell Vampiric Touch}
4th
{@spell Blight}, {@spell Death Ward}
5th
{@spell Antilife Shell}, {@spell Greater Restoration}

entries: Consider customizing how your spells look when you cast them. Your Witherbloom spells might rely on material components or a spellcasting focus drawn from the swamp environment of Witherbloom, and your spells might take on an appearance suggesting those natural elements. Spectral shapes of swamp animals or plants might form amid your spell effects.

entries.name: Building a Witherbloom Character
entries: Druids and warlocks make up most of Witherbloom's student body. A few wizards (mostly those who study the {@class Wizard|PHB|School of Necromancy|Necromancy|PHB}) and clerics (including those with the Divine Domains of {@class Cleric|PHB|Life|Life|PHB} or {@class Cleric|PHB|Nature|Nature|PHB}) also find their home in Witherbloom.
A number of rangers and barbarians study at Witherbloom as well, and some rogues learn how to create and use poisons during their studies at this college.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Students of Witherbloom College are equally likely to be found picking herbs for a healing tincture or riding zombified swamp beasts through the bayou. The Witherbloom Personality Traits table suggests a variety of traits you might adopt for your character.

entries.caption: Witherbloom Personality Traits
rows: I love brewing up a new recipe, even if some might be repulsed by my choice of ingredients. Or the final product. Or both.
My fashion sense is like my garden: withered, black, and weird.
I'm going to befriend every single monster in this swamp if it's the last thing I do.
Everything in this world dies eventually. The question is, what will you do with the time you have left?
I know we just met, but when you die, may I have your bones? For research.
Don't interrupt me; I'm brooding.

entries.name: Witherbloom Trinkets
entries: When you make your character, you may roll once on the {@item Witherbloom Trinket|SCC|Witherbloom Trinkets} table, instead of on the {@item trinket|phb|Trinkets table} in the {@book Player's Handbook|PHB}, for your starting trinket.

entries.name: Cultural Chameleon
entries: Before becoming an adventurer, you spent much of your adult life away from your homeland, living among people different from your kin. You came to understand these foreign cultures and the ways of their people, who eventually treated you as one of their own. One culture had more of an influence on you than any other, shaping your beliefs and customs. Choose a race whose culture you've adopted, or roll on the Adopted Culture table.

rows: Aarakocra
Dwarf

Goblin
Halfling
Human
Lizardfolk
Orc

entries.name: Feature: Adept Linguist
entries: You can communicate with humanoids who don't speak any language you know. You must observe the humanoids interacting with one another for at least 1 day, after which you learn a handful of important words, expressions, and gestures - enough to communicate on a rudimentary level.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Anthropologists leave behind the societies into which they were born to discover what life is like in other parts of the world. They seek to see how other races and civilizations survive - or why they did not. Some anthropologists are driven by intellectual curiosity, while others want the fame and recognition that comes with being the first to discover a new people, a lost tribe, or the truth about an ancient empire's downfall.

rows: I prefer the company of those who aren't like me, including people of other races
I'm a stickler when it comes to observing proper etiquette and local customs
I would rather observe than meddle
By living among violent people, I have become desensitized to violence.
I would risk life and limb to discover a new culture or unravel the secrets of a dead one.
When I arrive at a new settlement for the first time, I must learn all its customs.
Discovery. I want to be the first person to discover a lost culture. (Any)

Knowledge. By understanding other races and cultures, we learn to understand ourselves. (Any)
Power. Common people crave strong leadership, and I do my utmost to provide it. (Lawful)
Protection. I must do everything possible to save a society facing extinction. (Good)
Indifferent. Life is cruel. What's the point in saving people if they're going to die anyway? (Chaotic)
My mentor gave me a journal filled with lore and wisdom. Losing it would devastate me.
Having lived among the people of a primeval tribe or clan, I long to return and see how they are faring.
Years ago, tragedy struck the members of an isolated society I befriended, and I will honor them.
I want to learn more about a particular humanoid culture that fascinates me.
I seek to avenge a clan, tribe, kingdom, or empire that was wiped out.
I have a trinket that I believe is the key to finding a long-lost society.
Boats make me seasick.
I talk to myself, and I don't make friends easily.
I believe that I'm intellectually superior to people from other cultures and have much to teach them.
I've picked up some unpleasant habits living among goblins, lizardfolk, or orcs.
I complain about everything.
I wear a tribal mask and never take it off.

Avant de devenir aventurier, tu as passé une grande partie de ta vie adulte loin de ta terre natale, parmi des peuples différents du tien. Tu peux communiquer avec des humanoïdes qui ne parlent aucune des langues que tu connais. Tu dois observer les humanoïdes interagir entre eux pendant au moins 1 jour, après quoi tu apprends une poignée de mots, d'expressions et de gestes importants, suffisamment pour communiquer de façon rudimentaire.
Suggestions de caractéristiques

Les anthropologues quittent les sociétés où ils sont nés pour découvrir comment on vit dans d'autres régions du monde. Ils cherchent à voir comment d'autres races et civilisations survivent, ou pourquoi elles n'ont pas survécu. Certains anthropologues sont animés par la curiosité intellectuelle, tandis que d'autres veulent la célébrité et la reconnaissance qu'apporte le fait d'être le premier à découvrir un nouveau peuple, une tribu perdue ou la vérité sur la chute d'un empire antique.
Trait de personnalité
Je préfère la compagnie de ceux qui ne me ressemblent pas, y compris des personnes d'autres races
Je suis intransigeant sur le respect de l'étiquette et des coutumes locales
Je préfère observer plutôt que m'immiscer
À force de vivre parmi des gens violents, je suis devenu insensible à la violence.
Je risquerais ma vie et mon intégrité physique pour découvrir une nouvelle culture ou percer les secrets d'une culture disparue.
Lorsque j'arrive pour la première fois dans une nouvelle communauté, je dois apprendre toutes ses coutumes.
Idéal
Découverte. Je veux être la première personne à découvrir une culture perdue. (Tout alignement)
Distance. Il ne faut pas se mêler des affaires d'une autre culture, même si elle a besoin d'aide. (Loyal)
Connaissance. En comprenant les autres races et cultures, nous apprenons à nous comprendre nous-mêmes. (Tout alignement)
Pouvoir. Les gens du peuple aspirent à une autorité forte, et je fais tout mon possible pour la leur fournir. (Loyal)
Protection. Je dois faire tout mon possible pour sauver une société menacée de disparition. (Bon)
Indifférence. La vie est cruelle. À quoi bon sauver des gens s'ils doivent mourir de toute façon ? (Chaotique)
Lien
Mon mentor m'a donné un journal rempli de connaissances et de sagesse. Le perdre m'anéantirait.
Après avoir vécu parmi les membres d'une tribu ou d'un clan ancestral, je désire ardemment y retourner pour voir comment ils se portent.
Il y a des années, une tragédie a frappé les membres d'une société isolée avec lesquels j'avais noué des liens d'amitié, et je leur rendrai hommage.
Je veux en apprendre davantage sur une culture humanoïde particulière qui me fascine.
Je cherche à venger un clan, une tribu, un royaume ou un empire qui a été anéanti.
Je possède une babiole qui, selon moi, est la clé pour retrouver une société disparue depuis longtemps.

Je crois être intellectuellement supérieur aux personnes d'autres cultures et avoir beaucoup à leur apprendre.
J'ai pris de mauvaises habitudes en vivant parmi des gobelins, des hommes-lézards ou des orcs.
Je me plains de tout.

entries: Prior to becoming an adventurer, you spent most of your young life crawling around in the dust, pilfering relics of questionable value from crypts and ruins. Though you managed to sell a few of your discoveries and earn enough coin to buy proper adventuring gear, you have held onto an item that has great emotional value to you. entries.name: Feature: Historical Knowledge
entries: When you enter a ruin or dungeon, you can correctly ascertain its original purpose and determine its builders, whether those were dwarves, elves, humans, yuan-ti, or some other known race. In addition, you can determine the monetary value of art objects more than a century old.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Few archaeologists can resist the lure of an unexplored ruin or dungeon, particularly if such a site is the source of legends or is rumored to contain the treasures and relics of wizards, warlords, or royalty. Some archaeologists plunder for wealth or fame, while others consider it their calling to illuminate the past or keep the world's greatest treasures from falling into the wrong hands. Whatever their motivations, archaeologists combine the qualities of a scrappy historian with the self-made heroism of a treasure-hunting scoundrel.

rows: I love a good puzzle or mystery
I'm a pack rat who never throws anything away.
Fame is more important to me than money.
I have no qualms about stealing from the dead.
I'm happier in a dusty old tomb than I am in the centers of civilization.
Traps don't make me nervous. Idiots who trigger traps make me nervous.
I might fail, but I will never give up.
You might think I'm a scholar, but I love a good brawl. These fists were made for punching.
Preservation. That artifact belongs in a museum. (Good)
Greed. I won't risk my life for nothing. I expect some kind of payment. (Any)

Dignity. The dead and their belongings deserve to be treated with respect. (Lawful)
Immortality. All of my exploring is part of a plan to find the secret of everlasting life. (Any)
Danger. With every great discovery comes grave danger. The two walk hand in hand. (Any)
Ever since I was a child, I've heard stories about a lost city. I aim to find it, learn its secrets, and earn my place in the history books.
I want to find my mentor, who disappeared on an expedition some time ago.
I have a friendly rival. Only one of us can be the best, and I aim to prove it's me.
I won't sell an art object or other treasure that has historical significance or is one of a kind.
I'm secretly in love with the wealthy patron who sponsors my archaeological exploits.
I hope to bring prestige to a library, a museum, or a university.
I have a secret fear of some common wild animal - and in my work, I see them everywhere.
I can't leave a room without searching it for secret doors.
When I'm not exploring dungeons or ruins, I get jittery and impatient.
I have no time for friends or family. I spend every waking moment thinking about and preparing for my next expedition.
When given the choice of going left or right, I always go left.
I can't sleep except in total darkness.

texts.fr: Archéologue
Maîtrises de compétences :
{@skill History}, {@skill Survival}
Maîtrises d'outils :
{@item Cartographer's tools|phb} ou {@item navigator's tools|phb}
Langues :
Une au choix
Équipement :

Un {@item Map or Scroll Case|phb|étui en bois} contenant une carte menant à une ruine ou à un donjon, une {@item bullseye lantern|phb}, une {@item miner's pick|phb}, des {@item traveler's clothes|phb}, une {@item shovel|phb}, une {@item two-person tent|phb}, une {@item trinket|phb} récupérée sur un site de fouilles et une {@item pouch|phb} contenant 25 po
Fouilleur de poussière

Avant de devenir aventurier, tu as passé la majeure partie de ta jeunesse à ramper dans la poussière et à dérober des reliques de valeur douteuse dans des cryptes et des ruines. Même si tu as réussi à vendre certaines de tes découvertes et à gagner suffisamment d'argent pour acheter un véritable équipement d'aventurier, tu as conservé un objet d'une grande valeur sentimentale pour toi. Effectue un jet sur la table Objet emblématique pour découvrir ce que tu possèdes, ou choisis un objet dans la table.
Objet emblématique
Objet
{@item pole (10-foot)|phb|Perche de 10 pieds}
{@item Crowbar|phb}
Chapeau
{@item Hooded lantern|phb}
Médaillon
{@item Shovel|phb}
{@item Sledgehammer|phb}
{@item Whip|phb}
Aptitude : Connaissances historiques

Lorsque tu entres dans une ruine ou un donjon, tu peux en déterminer correctement la fonction d'origine et identifier ses bâtisseurs, qu'il s'agisse de nains, d'elfes, d'humains, de yuan-ti ou d'une autre race connue. De plus, tu peux déterminer la valeur monétaire des objets d'art vieux de plus d'un siècle.
Suggestions de caractéristiques

Peu d'archéologues peuvent résister à l'attrait d'une ruine ou d'un donjon inexploré, surtout si le lieu est à l'origine de légendes ou s'il est censé contenir les trésors et les reliques de magiciens, de seigneurs de guerre ou de membres de familles royales. Certains archéologues pillent pour s'enrichir ou devenir célèbres, tandis que d'autres considèrent qu'ils ont pour vocation d'éclairer le passé ou d'empêcher les plus grands trésors du monde de tomber entre de mauvaises mains. Quelles que soient leurs motivations, les archéologues allient les qualités d'un historien combatif à l'héroïsme d'un vaurien chasseur de trésors qui s'est fait tout seul.
